title: K8s node provisioning debug breadcrumbs - scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Playing back an incident where a subset of new node pools failed to join clusters after an automated upgrade job (autoscaler + machine image update).
- Symptoms: nodes stuck in NotReady or in ContainerCreating for core system pods (kube-proxy, aws-node) after provisioning.
- Repro: happens roughly 1/10 new nodes; seems correlated with kernel version mismatch and nodetool config timing during bootstrap.

What I tried (chronological notes / commands run + output snippets):

1) Confirm node condition and kubelet logs on a failing node - ssh to node (using bastion):
  ssh ec2-user@10.0.23.11
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail -n 80
  -> repeated failures: "failed to register node \"ip-10-0-23-11.ec2.internal\": node has no CPU capacity" then "error getting node info: node not found" (weird race).
  -> kernel: "audit: type=1400 ... apparmor=\"DENIED\" ..." (apparmor on nodes?)

2) kubectl get nodes -o wide and describe node
  kubectl get nodes | grep 10.0.23.11
  -> NotReady    40m    v1.24.8   ip-10-0-23-11   <none>   <none>

  kubectl describe node ip-10-0-23-11
  -> Conditions show KubeletReady False, NetworkUnavailable False, MemoryPressure False, DiskPressure False. Taints: None.
  -> Events: "Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up network for sandbox ... no network interface" repeated.

3) Check CNI plugin (aws-vpc-cni) logs on node
  sudo docker ps | grep aws-node || sudo crictl ps | grep aws-node
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | grep aws-node -C 4
  -> aws-node container kept restarting with error: "ENOTFOUND: route to gateway not found" and then crash.

4) Inspect cloud-init / user data bootstrap timing
  - Cloud-init logs show kubelet systemd unit starting before networkd has attached ENIs in some cases.
  - Hypothesis: IMDS / instance metadata available but ENI config not attached yet, so kubelet registers node without correct network interfaces -> CNI fails -> pods can't create sandbox -> node ends up NotReady.

5) Reproduced locally by forcing delayed eni attachment (used a test AMI):
  - Spin up node with sleep 30s before iptables rules are applied (added in cloud-init) -> same failure.

6) Quick mitigations attempted:
  - Add a systemd drop-in to kubelet.service to add "After=network-online.target" and "Wants=network-online.target". Restarted node: improved for one node but not deterministic across AZs.
  - Modified kubelet kube-reserved and system-reserved to be more conservative (reduce CPU pressure warnings). No clear impact on CNI failures.

7) Helm chart / kubeadm config checks
  - Checked our cluster-provisioner helm chart values (chart: cluster-autoscaler + node-bootstrap hooks). No changes to CNI daemonset.
  - Values of aws-vpc-cni: hostNetwork=false, init containers present. The init container uses iproute2 to configure IPs. If init container runs before ENI up, it will fail and restart -> pod stuck in CrashLoop.

8) More logs: kubelet register sequence (excerpt)
  - "Node registered with API server" followed by "Taint node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute added" then network errors in pod creation. Sequence suggests registration before CNI is ready.

Hypotheses / root cause theories:
- Race between kubelet node registration and cloud network (ENI) attach/config. If kubelet registers before ENI attached/route configured, CNI init containers fail to set up pod networking -> node appears NotReady for core pods and is effectively unusable.
- Some AMIs (kernel versions) trigger slower NIC driver bringup causing delay. Might be specific to 5.15 kernel build used in recent AMI image.
- Possible interplay with systemd ordering: network-online.target not guaranteed in all custom AMI cloud-init sequences.

Action items / next steps to validate and mitigate:
1) Add a small init script in cloud-init to wait for the primary ENI to be attached and for ip addr show to show the assigned IP before enabling kubelet.service. (Implement on test AMI only first.)
   - Command: "until ip addr show dev eth0 | grep -q \"inet \" ; do sleep 1; done" before starting kubelet.
2) Add kubelet systemd drop-in that depends on cloud-init target ordering. Investigate if network-online.target is provided by cloud-init-net or systemd-networkd in our images.
3) Add retry/backoff in CNI init containers to tolerate transient missing routes (change aws-vpc-cni init container script).
4) Run controlled rollout: replace AMI on a small test node pool with cloud-init fix, spin up 20 nodes across AZs and monitor join rate.
5) Add more detailed logging and a simple probe that checks ENI present before node registration (small sidecar or cloud-init sentinel file).

Notes / snippets to keep handy:
- kubectl describe node shows: "Failed to create pod sandbox: ... no network interface"
- kubelet journal: "failed to register node: node has no CPU capacity" -> weird transient when kubelet registers before node resources fully populated in cloud provider API.
- aws-vpc-cni init container log: "unable to find primary ENI index" -> indicates timing problem.

Slack / follow-ups:
- Pinged @Jordan and @Emily in #infra-provisioning on 2024-10-19 at 09:10 UTC. Linking notes in JIRA INFR-342 (provisioning flakiness).
- If we implement cloud-init wait, need QA with Dedicated clusters + Private on-prem packaging (different bootstrap flow).

Quick commands cheat-sheet (copy/paste):
- ssh to node: ssh ec2-user@<ip>
- kubelet logs: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 -o cat
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet | sed -n '1,200p'
- check ENI: ip addr show dev eth0; ip route show; sudo ethtool eth0
- cni logs: sudo crictl ps -a | grep aws-node; sudo crictl logs <container-id>
- describe node: kubectl describe node <node-name>
- check cloud-init: sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log; sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init.log

Random TODOs for follow-up PRs:
- [ ] Add ip wait to cloud-init for test AMI
- [ ] Add retry logic to aws-vpc-cni init container (small backoff loop)
- [ ] Add E2E test that simulates delayed ENI attach to catch regressions
- [ ] Document AMI kernel versions that are known-good vs flaky

Scratch / raw dumps (append-only):
- 2024-10-18 08:12 UTC: kubelet journal snippet: "W1018 08:12:21.123456   1234 kubelet_node_status.go:xxx] Failed to assign pod CIDR: timed out waiting for the condition"
- 2024-10-18 08:13 UTC: aws-vpc-cni init: "error getting local network config: primary ENI not found"
- 2024-10-19 09:15 UTC: attempted systemd drop-in, node recovered after reboot but two other AZs still saw failures.

If anyone picks this up: start with test AMI + cloud-init ip wait. I can push a minimal cloud-init diff and a test image build (AMI-qa-2024-10-20) and run a small pool. Ping me for access to the test account.

-- Sam
